[^trend]: Course calculation from nflverse play-by-play, regular seasons 1999–2025: called runs and passes (sacks and scrambles count as passes) in neutral situations (outside the last two minutes of each half, win probability 20–80%). EPA per play is nflverse's.

[^romer]: David Romer, "Do Firms Maximize? Evidence from Professional Football," *Journal of Political Economy* 114, no. 2 (2006): 340–365, https://eml.berkeley.edu/~dromer/papers/JPE_April06.pdf . Romer studied fourth downs in the 1998–2000 seasons and found choices systematically more conservative than the ones that maximized the chance of winning; one explanation he offers is that decision makers weigh the losses from failed gambles more heavily than the gains from successful ones.

[^quarters]: Course calculation from nflverse play-by-play, 2016–2025 regular seasons: designed runs and dropbacks on first and second down in neutral situations, EPA per play by quarter.

[^establish]: Course calculation from nflverse play-by-play: every regular-season team-game from 2016 to 2025 (5\,258 of them after leaving out ties). Designed runs are called runs, which include quarterback runs but not kneel-downs or scrambles. Correlations with winning (1 = won, 0 = lost): total runs 0\.49, first-half early-down run rate 0\.03, fourth-quarter run rate 0\.67. The point that rushing totals follow the score rather than cause it is an old one in football analytics; for the game-theory side of run-pass balance, see the Brian Burke essay listed under "Go deeper".

[^kcla]: Records and points from nflverse schedules (`load_schedules`), checked against Pro Football Reference: https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2018/ . Ranks for early-down pass rate and EPA are a course calculation (neutral situations, first and second down).

[^pers18]: Course calculation: nflverse participation data for 2018 (`load_participation`, from NFL Next Gen Stats), joined to regular-season runs and passes in nflverse play-by-play; personnel counted from the `offense_personnel` field. The first-and-10 pass rates by season are the chapter's own calculation (neutral situations, as in the first chart).

[^game54]: Rams 54, Chiefs 51, Monday, November 19, 2018, Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum (nflverse game `2018_11_KC_LA`; passing yards, touchdowns and the three defensive touchdowns from its play-by-play: Samson Ebukam's fumble return and interception return for the Rams, Allen Bailey's fumble return for the Chiefs). The game was scheduled for Estadio Azteca in Mexico City; on Tuesday, November 13, the league moved it after an inspection found the re-sodded Azteca surface did not meet NFL standards for playability and consistency: NFL.com, "Chiefs-Rams game moved from Mexico City to Los Angeles" (November 13, 2018), https://www.nfl.com/news/chiefs-rams-game-moved-from-mexico-city-to-los-angeles-0ap3000000988000 ; CBS Sports, "NFL moves Chiefs-Rams game from Mexico City to Los Angeles due to poor field conditions," https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/nfl-moves-chiefs-rams-game-from-mexico-city-to-los-angeles-due-to-poor-field-conditions/ .

[^bal19]: Pro Football Reference, 2019 Baltimore Ravens: https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/rav/2019.htm (14–2, 531 points); the 3,296 rushing yards broke the 1978 New England Patriots' NFL record of 3,165 in Week 17 and still stood after the 2025 season: NFL.com, "Ravens break single-season team rushing record" (December 29, 2019), https://www.nfl.com/news/ravens-break-single-season-team-rushing-record-0ap3000001092761 (nflverse play-by-play sums to 3,287, because a few plays are scored differently from the official totals); Lamar Jackson's 1,206 rushing yards broke Michael Vick's quarterback record of 1,039 (2006), and he was the second unanimous MVP after Tom Brady (2010), with all 50 first-place votes: CBS Sports, "NFL Honors: Lamar Jackson named unanimous 2019 NFL MVP," https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/nfl-honors-lamar-jackson-named-unanimous-2019-nfl-mvp-after-breakout-year-for-ravens-quarterback . Divisional round, January 11, 2020: Titans 28, Ravens 12 (nflverse schedules; Baltimore's early-down pass rate that night, 77%, from nflverse play-by-play, game `2019_19_TEN_BAL`). Early-down ranks are a course calculation.

[^cost]: Course calculation from nflverse play-by-play, 2021–2025 regular seasons, neutral situations between the offense's own 20 and the opponent's 30: the share of second-down and third-down snaps at each distance whose series ended in a first down or a touchdown (`series_success`, which counts fourth-down conversions too).

[^shot]: Course calculation from nflverse play-by-play, 2021–2025 regular seasons, neutral situations, second-and-1 to second-and-3: pass attempts with 15 or more air yards (`air_yards`, recorded only for throws), against designed runs and shorter throws. Play-action shares from FTN charting (`is_play_action`), 2022–2025, via nflreadpy.

[^alt]: Course calculation from nflverse play-by-play, 2021–2025 regular seasons, neutral situations: second downs whose previous snap, in the same drive, was the first-down play. "After a no-gain run" means the first-down play was a designed run and the distance is still 10. 1\,332 and 4\,179 snaps respectively.

[^serial]: Noha Emara, David Owens, John Smith and Lisa Wilmer, "Serial Correlation in National Football League Play Calling and Its Effects on Outcomes," *Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Economics* 69 (2017): 125–132, https://scholarship.haverford.edu/economics_facpubs/214 (working paper: https://mpra.ub.uni-muenchen.de/67862/). Using play-by-play from the 2000–2012 seasons, they found that NFL play-callers switch between runs and passes more often than an unpredictable caller would, and that the habit makes plays less effective.

[^zones]: Zone names and boundaries differ from staff to staff; "backed up," "coming out," "open field," "fringe" and "plus/minus territory" are common call-sheet and broadcast usage rather than rulebook terms. Coaches write field position as minus and plus yard lines (one backed-up objective in a clinic series with Steve Hauser: "avoid punting from the −1 to −4": Aidan Grabowski, "Teach Tapes with Steve Hauser (Week 8): Walking the Field – Backed Up," Coach and Coordinator, October 20, 2022, https://coachandcoordinator.com/?p=3907); some staffs call the deepest zone "coming off" (an indoor-football play-caller's breakdown in *Sports Illustrated*, March 24, 2017, https://www.si.com/ifl/2017/03/24/salt-lake-screaming-eagles-playcalling-goalpost); and four-down territory is also called the "dead zone" or "no man's land," with boundaries set by the kicker's range ("Dead zone (gridiron football)," Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_zone_%28gridiron_football%29). The 2025 kickoff touchback at the 35: NFL.com, "NFL owners vote to make dynamic kickoff permanent, adjust ball spot on touchbacks to 35-yard line" (2025), https://www.nfl.com/news/nfl-owners-vote-to-make-dynamic-kickoff-permanent-adjust-ball-spot-on-touchbacks-to-35-yard-line .

[^grounding]: NFL, *Official Playing Rules* (2026), Rule 8, Section 2, Article 1 (intentional grounding: a passer inside the tackle box may not throw an incomplete pass without a realistic chance of completion to avoid a loss of yardage; outside the box, the ball must reach the line of scrimmage; if the passer is in his own end zone, the penalty is a safety) and Rule 11, Section 5 (safety): <https://operations.nfl.com/the-rules/nfl-rulebook/> . The chapter on officiating, 09-04, walks through the tackle-box rule with a backed-up diagram.

[^punts]: Course calculation from nflverse play-by-play, 2021–2025 regular seasons: every punt, matched to the next run or pass in the same game; when that snap belonged to the other team, its yard line is where the opponent's drive started (returns, touchbacks, penalties and the occasional block or muff included).

[^fg50]: Course calculation from nflverse play-by-play, 2016 and 2025 regular seasons: field-goal attempts with a `kick_distance` of 50 yards or more, made or not (blocked kicks count as misses).

[^nfl4th]: Ben Baldwin, `nfl4th` (open-source fourth-down decision model, R package and public app, 2020–): https://github.com/nflverse/nfl4th ; the package site, with Baldwin's methodology and research notes: https://www.nfl4th.com/articles/4th-down-research.html . 10-04 uses the same model.

[^backed]: Course calculation from nflverse play-by-play, 2016–2025 regular seasons, neutral situations: first-and-10 snaps by field zone; shotgun from the play-by-play `shotgun` flag; sack rate = sacks per dropback.

[^fourth]: Course calculation from nflverse play-by-play, 2025 regular season: fourth downs with 3 or fewer yards to go, outside the last two minutes of each half, counting runs and passes as "go for it" against punts and field-goal attempts.

[^det]: Records, points and playoff results from nflverse schedules, checked against Pro Football Reference: https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/det/2023.htm and https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/det/2024.htm . NFC Championship, January 28, 2024: 49ers 34, Lions 31; divisional round, January 18, 2025: Commanders 45, Lions 31. Fourth-down attempts (all game states, runs and passes) and early-down ranks are a course calculation. Ben Johnson was Detroit's offensive coordinator from 2022 to 2024 and became the Bears' head coach in 2025 (see the course fact sheet).

[^starts]: Course calculation from nflverse play-by-play, 2025 regular season: the yard line of each drive's first scrimmage snap. 66% of drives began at the offense's own 25 or beyond (70% in 2024, when the end-zone touchback came out to the 30).
